answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before accepting work. Whether an agent maps tundra, tracks willow growth, or identifies ivory, the same bond applies, and one deposit cannot back multiple identities. An attacker spawning 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month. New names are cheap, but each usable identity consumes additional capital and incurs its financing cost.
